title: Pork and Beans
description: Prepared with pork, beans, and water.
steps: Soak the meat all night in a pan of cold water.
Put the beans into a pot with cold water, and let them hang all night over the embers of the fire, or set them in the chimney corner, that they may warm as well as soak.
Early in the morning rinse them through a cullender.
Having scored the rind of the pork, (which should not be a very fat piece,) put it into a pot with cold water, and boil it till tender, carefully skimming off the liquid fat.
In another pot boil the beans till they have all bursted.
When soft, take them up; lay the pork in a tin pan; and cover it with the beans, adding a very little water.
Bake them in an oven till brown, but not longer.

description: A pudding made with pork, split peas, and water.
steps: Soak the pork, which should not be a fat piece, over night in cold water.
In another pan soak a quart of dried split peas.
In the morning put on the peas to boil slowly until tender.

description: A pastry dish made with pork, fat, and onion.

ingredients.name: two and a half to three pounds of the thick ends of a loin of pork

steps: Make a good plain paste.

title: Pot Roast (Old Style)
description: Prepared with beef, onion, and water.

ingredients.name: a piece of fresh beef weighing about five or six pounds

steps: Take a piece of fresh beef weighing about five or six pounds that is not too fat
Wash it and put it into a pot with barely sufficient water to cover it
Set it over a slow fire
After it has stewed an hour salt and pepper it
Stew it slowly until tender, adding a little onion if liked
Do not replenish the water at the last, but let all nearly boil away
When tender all through take the meat from the pot and pour the gravy in a bowl
Put a large lump of butter in the bottom of the pot
Dredge the piece of meat with flour and return it to the pot to brown, turning it often to prevent its burning
Take the gravy that you have poured from the meat into the bowl and skim off all the fat
Pour this gravy in with the meat and stir in a large spoonful of flour wet with a little water
Let it boil up ten or fifteen minutes and pour into a gravy dish
Serve both hot, the meat on a platter

title: Potato Croquettes No. 1
description: Prepared with potatoes, bread crumbs, and lard.

ingredients.name: butter (a lump half the size of an egg)

steps: Wash, peel and put four large potatoes in cold water, with a pinch of salt, and set them over a brisk fire.

Take another saucepan, and put in it ten tablespoonfuls of milk and a lump of butter half the size of an egg; put it over a brisk fire.

title: Preserved Cantaloupes

title: Preserved Citron or Water-Melon Rind
description: Prepared with water, citron or water or melon or rind, and lemon juice.
steps: Pare off the green skin, and the soft, white, inner rind.
Cut into strips or into fanciful shapes.
Allow a pound and a quarter of sugar to each pound of rind.
Line your kettle with vine leaves and fill with the rind, scattering a little pulverized alum over each layer.

Take out your rind, which should be well greened by this process, and throw at once into very cold water.
It should lie in soak, changing the water every hour, for four hours.
For the syrup, allow two cups of water to a pound and a quarter of sugar.
Boil, and skim it until no more scum comes up; put in the rind, and simmer gently nearly an hour.
Take it out, and spread upon dishes in the sun until firm and almost cool.
Simmer in the syrup for half an hour; spread out again, and, when firm, put into a large bowl, and pour over it the scalding syrup.

title: Preserved Cucumbers
description: Prepared with cucumbers, lemon-peel, and lemon.

ingredients.name: juice and grated peel of lemons

steps: Your cucumbers should be well shaped, and all of the same size.
Spread the bottom and sides of a preserving kettle with a thick layer of vine leaves.
Put in the cucumbers with a little alum broken small.
Cover them thickly with vine leaves, and then with a dish.
Fill up the kettle with water, and let them hang over a slow fire till next morning, but do not allow the water to boil.
Next day, take them out, cool them, and repeat the process with fresh vine leaves, till the cucumbers are a fine green.
When cold drain them, cut a small piece out of the flat side, and extract the seeds.
Wipe the cucumbers in a dry cloth, and season the inside with a mixture of bruised mace and grated lemon-peel.
Tie on with a pack-thread the bit that was cut out.
Weigh them, and to every pound of cucumbers allow a pound of loaf-sugar.

Strain the syrup all over the cucumbers, and put them up in glass jars.

title: Preserved Green Tomatoes
description: Prepared with tomatoes, lemons, and sugar.

title: Preserved Lemons
description: Prepared with lemons, lemon-juice, and white of egg.
steps: Take large fine ripe lemons, that have no blemishes, choosing those with thin, smooth rinds.
With a sharp knife scoop a hole in the stalk end of each, large enough to admit the handle of a tea-spoon.
Put them into a preserving kettle with clear water, and boil them gently till you find them tender, keeping the kettle uncovered.
Take them out, drain, and cool them, and put them into a small tub.
Prepare a thin syrup of a pound of loaf-sugar to a quart of water.
Boil and skim it, and pour it over the lemons and cover them.
Let them stand in the syrup till next day.
Pour the syrup from the lemons, and spread them on a large dish.
Boil it a quarter of an hour, and pour it over them again, having first returned them to the tub.
Cover them, and let them again stand till next day.
Boil the syrup and pour it over them again.
Repeat this process every day till you find that the lemons are quite clear, and that the syrup has penetrated them thoroughly.
If the syrup becomes too weak, add a little more sugar to it.

Finally, make a strong syrup in the proportion of half a pint of water to a pound of sugar, adding a jill of raw lemon-juice squeezed from fresh lemons, and allowing to every two pounds of sugar the beaten white of an egg.
Mix all well together in the kettle.
Boil and skim it, and when the scum ceases to rise, pour the syrup boiling hot over the lemons; and covering them closely, let them stand undisturbed for four days.
Look at them, and if you find that they have not sucked in enough of the syrup to make the inside very sweet, boil them gently in the syrup for a quarter of an hour.
When they are cold, put them up in glass jars.

steps: Change the water nearly every hour

Put in the limes and pour on as much clear cold water as will cover them
Fill up with a very thick layer of vine-leaves
Boil them slowly an hour or more

They must boil till a twig can pierce them
After greening, give the kettle a complete washing or take another
Weigh the limes and allow to every pound of them a pound of the best double refined loaf-sugar and half a pint of very clear water
Break up the sugar and put it into the kettle
Pour on the water, which must previously be mixed with some beaten white of egg, allowing the white of one egg to three pounds of sugar
Let the sugar dissolve in the water before setting it over the fire, stirring it well
Boil and skim the sugar, and when the scum ceases to rise, put in the limes
Add the juice that was saved from them, strained from the pulp, seeds, &c.
Boil the limes in the syrup till they are very tender and transparent
Take them out carefully and spread them on flat dishes
Put the syrup into a tureen and leave it uncovered for two days

Cut them in half and squeeze them through a strainer into a pitcher

title: Preserved Water-Melon Rind
description: Prepared with water, white of egg, and lemon-juice.
steps: Having pared off the green skin, cut the rind of a water-melon into pieces of any shape you please (stars, diamonds, circles, crescents or leaves)
Weigh the pieces, and allow to each pound a pound and a half of loaf sugar

description: A pudding made with prunes, cream or sauce or butter or sugar or nutmeg, and flour.

title: Puff Paste
description: Prepared with pastry, butter, and water.
steps: Wash the butter, pat and fold until no water flies.
Reserve two tablespoons of butter, and shape remainder into a circular piece one-half inch thick, and put on floured board.
Work two tablespoons of butter into flour with the tips of fingers of the right hand.
Moisten to a dough with cold water, turn on slightly floured board, and knead one minute.
Cover with towel, and let stand five minutes.
Pat and roll one-fourth inch thick, keeping paste a little wider than long, and corners square.
If this cannot be accomplished with rolling-pin, draw into shape with fingers.
Place butter on centre of lower half of paste.
Cover butter by folding upper half of paste over it.
Press edges firmly, to enclose as much air as possible.
Fold right side of paste over enclosed butter, the left side under enclosed butter.
Turn paste half-way round, cover, and let stand five minutes.
Pat, and roll one-fourth inch thick, having paste longer than wide, lifting often to prevent paste from sticking, and dredging board slightly with flour when necessary.
Fold from ends towards centre, making three layers.
Cover, and let stand five minutes.
Repeat twice, turning paste half-way round each time before rolling.
After fourth rolling, fold from ends to centre, and double, making four layers.
Put in cold place to chill; if outside temperature is not sufficiently cold, fold paste in a towel, put in a dripping-pan, and place between dripping pans of crushed ice.
If paste is to be kept for several days, wrap in a napkin, put in tin pail and cover tightly, then put in cold place; if in ice box, do not allow pail to come in direct contact with ice.

title: Pumpkin Chips
description: Prepared with pumpkin, lemons, and lemon-juice.
steps: Take a fine pumpkin of a rich deep colour, pare off the outer rind
